facts.heading: Anxiety worsened in September
facts.content: Hannah feels anxious all the time, and this feeling got worse in September.
facts.evidence: I think I'm just anxious all the time and it got worse in September.

facts.heading: Took on deputy head role
facts.content: Hannah has taught at her school for 11 years. She was asked to step up when the deputy head left.
facts.evidence: I've taught here for 11 years and then they had asked me to step up and when our deputy left.

facts.heading: Fear of being incompetent
facts.content: Hannah worries that people will notice she doesn't know what she is doing.
facts.evidence: I keep thinking they picked the wrong person, and that sooner or later someone will notice I have no idea what I'm doing.

facts.heading: Anxiety manifests Sunday evenings
facts.content: On Sunday evenings, Hannah's chest tightens, and she starts rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in her head.
facts.evidence: Mostly Sunday evenings, my chest goes tight and I start rehearsing Monday's staff meeting in my head.

facts.heading: Imagined negative judgment
facts.content: Hannah rehearses every possible question and what she would say, and what others would think if she got it wrong.
facts.evidence: Every possible question someone might ask and what I would say, then what they would think of me if I got it wrong.

facts.heading: Fears being seen as inadequate
facts.content: Hannah imagines people thinking she is out of her depth or that they gave the job to a teacher who can't read.
facts.evidence: That I'm out of my depth.

facts.heading: Rewrote email to governors
facts.content: Last week, Hannah rewrote the same email to the governors four times.
facts.evidence: Last week I rewrote the same email to the governors four times.

facts.heading: Fear of Mr. Hargraves' opinion
facts.content: Hannah was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think she was stupid regarding the behavior policy email.
facts.evidence: I was afraid Mr. Hargraves, the chair of governors, would think that I was stupid.

facts.heading: Feels like she is pretending
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is lying to Mr. Hargraves about being capable.
facts.evidence: About being capable, as if I'm pretending.

facts.heading: Feels like wearing mother's coat
facts.content: Hannah feels like a child wearing her mother's coat.
facts.evidence: Most days I feel like a child wearing her mother's coat.

facts.heading: Mother was a headteacher
facts.content: Hannah's mother was a headteacher for 20 years.
facts.evidence: My mum's, I suppose. She was a headteacher for 20 years.

facts.heading: Comparing herself to mother
facts.content: Hannah compares herself to her mother, thinking everything she does, her mother would have done better.
facts.evidence: Everything I do, I think, would she have done it better?

facts.heading: Mother's supportive nature
facts.content: Hannah's mother is supportive on the surface.
facts.evidence: She is very supportive on the surface.

facts.heading: Mother dismisses her worries
facts.content: Hannah's mother tells her that she has always worried too much and should stop being silly.
facts.evidence: She says I've always worried too much and I should stop being silly.

facts.heading: Hides feelings from mother
facts.content: Hannah feels like she is making a fuss when her mother suggests she should stop worrying, so she doesn't tell her how bad it is.
facts.evidence: It makes me feel like I'm making a fuss, so I don't tell her how bad it is.

facts.heading: Awake at 4 AM daily
facts.content: Hannah is awake at 4 AM every morning.
facts.evidence: I'm awake at 4 every morning

facts.heading: Waking up with to-do list

facts.evidence: Then I'm awake at 4 going through the to-do list

facts.evidence: Timetable changes, the offset prep, a parent complaint, a child I'm worried about

facts.heading: Waking pattern started in term
facts.content: Hannah has been waking like this since about the second week of term.
facts.evidence: Since about the second week of term

facts.evidence: I drink a lot of coffee to get through a day

facts.evidence: Five or six

facts.evidence: My heart goes fast.

facts.evidence: So you lost some company along with the promotion?

facts.evidence: Then I went home and cried
